move: blurred percentage sharpens as it counts to 100, snaps, dissolves back
how: A 300px three-digit percentage on black with a blue halo and a thin progress bar. A state value tweens 0 to 100 over 3.1s (power3.out) from 0.07D and is written into the digits each seek; the whole number starts at blur(28px), scale 1.12, opacity 0.6 and resolves to sharp over 3.2s (power2.out), the label fades in with an 8px blur, and the halo scales 0.6 to 1.2. The changing units digit gets a tiny 6px re-blur that decays until its next change. At 0.85D the number pops to 1.04 and settles with elastic.out(1,0.5); at 0.93D the whole block blurs to 24px and fades to 0.
adapt: Change the label, the target value, the accent halo colour and the digit font; keep the 3.1s power3.out count and the 3.2s blur resolve that make it feel like focus pulling.
port: mount(el, shot) appends .halo, .num digits, .lbl and .bar; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline plus an onUpdate on the state tween that writes digit text, per-digit blur and bar width (the __fx.seek override). Scope '#d0..d2', '#bar', '.num', '.wrap' to el.
caveats: ends faded to opacity 0 while it starts at opacity 0.6 blurred, so the loop point is a soft cut, not identical
animated filter: blur() on 300px text is slow to render
